refs.quote: VIMPAT is indicated for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 1 month of age and older.

Adults (17 years and older): Initial dosage for monotherapy for the treatment of partial-onset seizures is 100 mg twice daily ( 2.1 ) Initial dosage for adjunctive therapy for the treatment of partial-onset seizures or primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures is 50 mg twice daily ( 2.1 ) Maximum recommended dosage for monotherapy and adjunctive therapy is 200 mg twice daily ( 2.1 )

regimens.dose_text: Initial dosage for monotherapy is 100 mg orally twice daily (200 mg/day). Titrate based on clinical response and tolerability, no more frequently than once per week, up to a maximum recommended dosage of 200 mg twice daily (400 mg/day).

regimens.indication: Partial-Onset Seizures and Primary Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures (Adjunctive Therapy)

refs.quote: VIMPAT is indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients 4 years of age and older.

Initial dosage for adjunctive therapy for the treatment of partial-onset seizures or primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures is 50 mg twice daily ( 2.1 ) Maximum recommended dosage for monotherapy and adjunctive therapy is 200 mg twice daily ( 2.1 )

regimens.dose_text: Initial dosage for adjunctive therapy is 50 mg orally twice daily (100 mg/day). May increase weekly by 50 mg twice daily based on clinical response up to a maximum recommended dosage of 200 mg twice daily (400 mg/day).

regimens.indication: Rapid Maintenance Target / Acute Status Epilepticus Loading Dose

refs.quote: The loading dose should be administered with medical supervision because of the possibility of increased incidence of adverse reactions, including central nervous system (CNS) and cardiovascular adverse reactions [see Warnings and Precautions (5.2 , 5.3) , Adverse Reactions (6.1) , and Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .

Injection: for intravenous use only when oral administration is temporarily not feasible; the recommended dosage is based on body weight and is administered two or three times daily over 15 to 60 minutes; obtaining ECG before initiation is recommended in certain patients ( 2.7 , 5.3 )

regimens.dose_text: Single IV loading dose of 200 mg infused over 15 to 60 minutes under medical supervision (consider baseline ECG), followed 12 hours later by 100 mg twice daily (200 mg/day). In refractory status epilepticus protocols, guidelines endorse up to 400 mg IV.

refs.locator: Section 2.5 Dosage Information for Patients with Renal Impairment
refs.quote: For patients with severe renal impairment [creatinine clearance (CL CR ) less than 30 mL/min as estimated by the Cockcroft-Gault equation for adults; CL CR less than 30 mL/min/1.73m 2 as estimated by the Schwartz equation for pediatric patients] or end-stage renal disease, a reduction of 25% of the maximum dosage is recommended.

hepatic.value: For patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment, a reduction of 25% of the maximum dosage is recommended. The dose initiation and titration should be based on clinical response and tolerability in patients with hepatic impairment. VIMPAT use is not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

In vitro electrophysiological studies have shown that lacosamide selectively enhances slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels, resulting in stabilization of hyperexcitable neuronal membranes and inhibition of repetitive neuronal firing.

mg_safety.note: Lacosamide selectively enhances slow sodium channel inactivation and does not impair neuromuscular transmission; safe in myasthenia gravis

value.instructions: VIMPAT tablets may be crushed and mixed with water for enteral feeding tube administration. VIMPAT oral solution (10 mg/mL) is also available and can be administered via nasogastric or gastrostomy tube.

lactation_summary.value: Lacosamide is present in human milk; reports describe increased sleepiness in breastfed infants. Monitor nursing infants closely.
